sections.title: Letter G Sound
paragraphs: The letter (G) /dʒ/ usually makes the sound /ɡ/, as in the word (game) /ɡeɪm/, which means game. Across English words, this letter makes three different sounds, and it can also be silent.

sections.title: How to Say
paragraphs: For the first sound, press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Release the air with your voice. For the second sound, touch your tongue tip behind your top front teeth. Push air through while your vocal cords vibrate. For the third sound, round your lips slightly and let voiced air flow smoothly over your tongue. Feel your throat vibrate for all three sounds.

sections.title: Reading and Spelling
paragraphs: Before the vowels a, o, or u, before consonants, or at the end of a word, it makes the sound /ɡ/, like in (gas) /ɡæs/. Often before e, i, or y, it makes the sound /dʒ/, like in (gem) /dʒɛm/. In some borrowed words before e or i, it makes the sound /ʒ/, like in (genre) /ʒɒn.rə/. It is not pronounced before the letter n, like in (sign) /saɪn/.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
paragraphs: Do not swallow the hard sound or make it rough in your throat. Keep the contact firm against the roof of your mouth, just like the sound in the word go. When it is soft, make sure you add your voice, so it does not sound like church. In words where the letter stands before n, remember to keep it completely silent.
